title: Risk-to-reward planning
summary: Before entering, set the stop where the idea is wrong and a target, then compare the distances. A 2:1 plan risks 1 to aim for 2.
unreliableWhen: A planned ratio says nothing about how often the target is reached. Targets placed far beyond any recent move, or stops squeezed to make the ratio look good, distort the plan.
goodExample: Stop below the swing low 30 pips away, target at the next resistance 60 pips away: 2:1, decided before entry.
badExample: Moving the stop closer to make a 3:1 ratio, inside normal candle movement.

chart.lookFor: Mark an entry after the pullback, a stop below the swing low and a target at the earlier high. Measure both distances and compare the stop with ATR 14.
